Two paragraphs

This paragraph runs the whole width of a wide window, so its lines are far too long to read with comfort. The eye has to travel a long way back to find the start of the next line, and it often lands on the wrong one. That is why reading text is given a maximum width, and why the guide asks for it to be measured rather than guessed. Here it has none at all.

This paragraph has a maximum width, so its lines stay short enough to read with comfort, and the eye finds the start of each new line without searching. It is long enough to run over several lines, which is what the measure needs to see.
